groups.defect: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of the credential's userId as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the wrong calcomUserId.
groups.rationale: All seven point at the same call (lines 85-94) and report the same wrong argument, with the same fix.

groups.defect: The Google Calendar refresh saves the whole SafeParse result ({success, data}) as credential.key instead of its .data.
groups.rationale: All five report the same wrapped-object persistence bug at the same lines, with the same fix (use .data).

groups.defect: In sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but callers (Google, HubSpot, zohocrm, zoho-bigin) expect their old shape (.data or a token object), so they fail.
groups.rationale: One root cause in the helper's return shape. Some members point at the helper or at several callers, others only at the Google caller.

groups.defect: throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam only runs on the non-team path with teamId null, so non-admin team members can create team credentials.
groups.rationale: Both report the same misplaced admin check in createOAuthAppCredential, with the same fix.

groups.defect: The webhook secret is compared with non-constant-time !==. In addition, zod .parse and the decrypt/JSON.parse step throw unhandled 500s on malformed input instead of returning 400s.
groups.rationale: Both report the timing-unsafe secret comparison. s_6431b4bc adds the unhandled-parse defect.

groups.defect: The computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema collapse to the literal '[object Object]', so expiry fields and refresh_token are stripped. The function also always fills in the placeholder 'refresh_token', which overwrites real tokens.
groups.rationale: Both report the same broken computed-key schema and the placeholder refresh_token, in parseRefreshTokenResponse.
